Zlatan Ibrahimovic, a former Barcelona and Inter Milan player, stated that top players personally put more pressure on themselves, and also commented on social media's role in football.

A 73-year-old fisherman in Brazil discovered a metal object, later confirmed to be a payload shroud from a European satellite launched last July, floating in a remote river and it took a team of over 10 people to retrieve it.

Former Labour government minister James Purnell warned that downgrading the licence fee to a civil offence could lead to the loss of around £35m, equivalent to the cost of taking off air BBC Four, and would force the government to choose between taking the affected services off air or increasing the licence fee.

Harps secured a win over Derry, with David Scully scoring the first goal and Ryan Curran doubling the lead on 75 minutes, as they earned their first win over Derry since 1998 on their first Premier Division game since 2008.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced that issuers of digital coins, known as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register their offers and sales in the same way as traditional securities sales to protect investors and the integrity of the markets.

Operation Anagram, a police operation formed in 2006, has helped piece together a timeline of serial killer Peter Tobin's movements and relationships, leading to the conviction of Tobin for the murders of three women, and will continue to monitor new information and assist in bringing closure to families of potential other victims.

Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel said that beating Mercedes "is not easy at all", while Mercedes' Lewis Hamilton acknowledged that Ferrari "did a better job" than Mercedes in the Australian Grand Prix, but expressed confidence that Mercedes can improve and be ahead in future races.

A woman has accused former show business agent Max Clifford of indecent assault in his London office in the 1980s, with Clifford denying the allegations and responding with "no comment" to some of the questions during his police interview.
Ospreys coach Steve Tandy is expecting a physically intense match against the Scarlets on Boxing Day, as his team looks to close the gap to the Scarlets in the Pro12 table.

The city of Leicester hosted a large-scale Diwali celebration, believed to be one of the biggest outside India, with a lights switch-on event attracting about 35,000 people, and featuring a firework display, entertainment on stage in the park, and other events.

The parents of Rosie Ross, who was killed by Inderjit Kainth in May 2001, are planning to wind down the charity Rosie's Helping Hands after 16 years since Rosie's death, but will continue to fundraise and help projects until summer 2017.

Cwm Taf Health Board and Macmillan Cancer Support are seeking planning permission to build a £5 million state-of-the-art specialist unit at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital, which would provide inpatient, outpatient, and day palliative care for incurable cancer, and work is expected to start later this year.

The Columba Declaration, authored by the Reverend John McPake and Bishop Peter Forster, commits the Church of England and the Church of Scotland to "grow together in communion" and to strengthen their partnership in mission, with the new arrangements including a small contact group that meets yearly and reports to the ecumenical bodies within each Church.
Ben Parkinson, a Doncaster-based soldier who was seriously injured in a bomb attack in Afghanistan, has received thousands of friend requests on Facebook after carrying the Olympic torch.

Five Saudis, including a reported prince, were detained at Beirut's airport after two tonnes of Captagon pills, which are consumed widely in the Middle East, were found in cases due to be loaded onto a private jet.

Police are investigating allegations related to the charity Kids Company, which provides support to vulnerable children, and are urging anyone with information or concerns to contact them or the NSPCC.

The Queen, who turns 90, is described by her cousin Margaret Rhodes as "full of laughter" and possessing a good sense of humour, with the ability to imitate local accents from different parts of the UK.

A report by the UN Agency for Human Settlements (UN-Habitat) finds that Latin America is the world's most urbanized region, with nearly nine out of 10 people expected to live in cities by 2050, but also notes that the region struggles with extremely high income inequality, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%.

A Labour councillor in Carmarthenshire, Tegwen Devichand, shared a Facebook post from a far-right group, Britain First, and later said she did not remember sharing it, with Plaid Cymru accusing Labour members of working with UKIP to undermine the council's decision, while the Welsh Labour party stated that an investigation into the matter was underway.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by relatives of British troops killed in the conflict, has now received enough backing to fund the whole campaign, allowing its lawyers to analyze the Chilcot report and provide guidance on whether legal action against key people involved in the 2003 invasion would succeed or not.

A judge in Baltimore has allowed Syed's defence team to submit new evidence, including arguments about the reliability of mobile phone records and testimony from a potential alibi, in a bid to revisit the 1999 case of his life sentence for the death of Hae Min Lee.

A 16-year-old boy, who had previously been convicted of assaults, pleaded guilty to assault after pulling a machete on a taxi driver during a dispute over fare payment, with sentence deferred until next month.

John Clancy, a Labour councillor and former teacher, has been elected as the new leader of Birmingham City Council, replacing Sir Albert Bore, and will officially take the position on December 1 after winning the ballot by a single vote.

Roger Moore discussed his early meetings with Bond film director Guy Hamilton, where they aimed to avoid comparisons to previous Bond actor Sean Connery, and producer Barbara Broccoli recalled how Connery's casting broke the traditional image of a British leading man.

Historic England is calling for people to document "witches' marks," ancient symbols carved into buildings to protect inhabitants and visitors from witches and evil spirits, which can be found in various locations, including medieval houses, churches, and other buildings, most commonly from around 1550 to 1750.
During an unusual exchange at Prime Minister's Questions, Jeremy Corbyn referred to Baldrick's line "Our cunning plan is to have no plan" from the 1980s TV show Blackadder.

A UK judge has ruled in favor of a passenger who claimed compensation for a delayed flight, stating that "justice delayed is justice denied," which is likely to encourage thousands of similar claims against airlines such as Jet2, Thomas Cook, and Ryanair.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, stated that the UK's loss of control means the EU could dictate the movement of jobs out of London after Brexit, while France offers incentives such as lower taxes, easier hiring and firing, English law courts, and English-speaking schools to attract businesses.

China has deployed surface-to-air missiles on the disputed island of Woody or Yongxing Island in the Paracels, according to satellite images, prompting concerns from the US and other nations over the increasing militarization of the South China Sea.

Scientists have discovered that Adanson's house spider uses its silk draglines to stabilize and brake during jumps, allowing it to land poised and ready to pounce on prey, and this finding could inspire the design of new, agile robots.

The Supreme Court ruled that the UK government is not legally compelled to consult the Welsh assembly on Brexit, and it is likely that AMs would get a vote on the triggering process, with the assembly agreeing that it does not have a power of veto.

The Co-op Bank, which was forced to seek a buyer due to regulatory concerns, has now reached a "substantially agreed" recapitalization plan with existing investors, a significant step towards resolving its financial issues.

NRW estimates that the Swansea tidal lagoon project would mean 21% of salmon and 25% of sea trout dying each year, as they migrate to and from local rivers, while the project's developer, TLP, disputes these figures, citing computer modelling that estimated a "worst case scenario" of the lagoon killing 2% of all species of fish.

The article discusses and mocks various contestants' mistakes and failures on a reality TV show, including a hypnotherapist's outdated advice, sexist game questions, and a coach tour guide getting lost, among other humorous moments.

The UK's immigration cap, which limits the number of "tier 2" visas issued to skilled workers from non-EU countries, has been deemed "counter-productive" by a parliamentary committee, as it led to a large number of rejected applications from nurses and a crisis in the NHS was averted by emergency measures.

Jake Vallely, 24, has been convicted of punching and beating 20-year-old Private Matthew Boyd, a soldier from the Royal Gibraltar Regiment, outside a bar in Brecon, with Vallely's sentencing set for December 8.

The BBC, in collaboration with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to select programs on an experimental version of the iPlayer on-demand platform using their mind, with potential applications for people with disabilities.

The Welsh education system has been criticized for potentially stifling the progress of more able learners due to the focus on meeting specific performance measures, such as achieving five GCSEs at grade A*-C, which can lead to a lack of support for students who could excel at higher grades.

A new posthumous album, "Out Among the Stars," featuring 12 unreleased tracks by Johnny Cash, will be released in March, including duets with June Carter and Waylon Jennings, after being discovered in a vault in 2012 by Cash's son, John Carter Cash.

A tribunal found that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed from the Ardoyne Association due to her role as primary carer for her disabled daughter, in contravention of the Disability Discrimination Act 1995, and the Court of Appeal upheld the decision.
Rangers have signed 30-year-old Scottish midfielder Graham Dorrans on a three-year deal, becoming manager Pedro Caixinha's ninth summer signing.

Team Brewster, skipped by Eve Muirhead's brother, secured the men's spot at the European Championships by defeating Olympic silver medallists David Murdoch's team 7-2 and 9-5, while Eve Muirhead's rink claimed the women's place with three wins in a best-of-five tournament decider.

Councillor Pierre Oxley has called for a scrutiny meeting to discuss concerns about the proposed Holland Haven-to-Clacton defences, and was accused by Conservative councillor Peter Halliday of "scaremongering".

Dundee Football Club's American owners, John Nelms and Tim Keyes, plan to submit a land use application for 29 acres of land in Camperdown Park to potentially improve the club's stadium and facilities.

Chris Froome finished third in the general classification of the Criterium du Dauphine, two seconds behind the group that finished behind Movistar stage winner Jesus Herrada, and is now 13 seconds off the overall leader Alberto Contador.

The bodies of Sian Blake, a 43-year-old former EastEnders actress, and her two sons, Zachary and Amon, were found in the garden of their home in south-east London, with all three confirmed to have died from head and neck injuries, after a triple murder inquiry was launched following their disappearance on December 13.

Wimbledon organisers have decided to play on the traditional rest day, Sunday, with at least eight singles' matches, to avoid sections of the draw getting too far apart and to catch up on a backlog of matches that had built up due to play being stopped 10 times in five days.

Dick Advocaat, the 68-year-old manager of Sunderland, has made the decision to leave the club after eight games, citing a desire to give everyone time to turn things around and to fulfil a promise to his wife, despite initially agreeing to stay on and later signing a new one-year contract.

Russia's government expects a 0.8% decline in GDP next year, and the rouble has fallen to a rate of 57 to the dollar, from an unspecified rate, a fall of more than 6%, due to an oil price slump and Western sanctions.

Kenyan opposition leader Raila Odinga has decided to take his election claims to the Supreme Court, claiming the opposition has collected concrete evidence of massive irregularities, while foreign observers described the election as free and fair.

A 60-year-old certified scuba diver died while underwater at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland after being unable to be revived, with CPR efforts performed by a nurse and then a doctor on board the vessel.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have agreed a £3.7m contract to continue Loganair's direct air service from Dundee to London Stansted for another two years, with the UK government contributing 50% of the funding.

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is launching its video streaming service in China through its Chinese partner PPTV, marking the first time an entire channel devoted to WWE will be available, with industry-watchers saying that finding local stars will be key to its success.

Three Birmingham men, including a 28-year-old West Midlands police officer, are being questioned on suspicion of conspiracy to pervert the course of justice and other charges after a hoax tip-off led to a police alert and increased security measures for officers.
Ireland secured a 4-1 victory over Poland in their quarter-final match, with Craig Fulton's team advancing to the semi-finals where they will face Wales.

Philip Craig, 38, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 25 years for the murder of Christopher Laskaris, 24, after he stabbed him to death and then returned to the flat to steal valuables, including a TV and guitars.

The Metropolitan Police Service has closed its reinvestigation into the 2010 death of Kester David, a 53-year-old man found badly burned under a bridge, and apologized to his family, concluding that there was no evidence of foul play despite previous allegations that he was killed due to working as a police informant.

UK sports events saw a total attendance less than the 75 million recorded in 2012, with football being the overall winner in attendance stakes at 43.4 million, and horseracing events among the top 10 best attended showpieces.

The Scottish National Party has challenged Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn's position as the official opposition, citing Labour's loss of two-thirds of its shadow cabinet and Corbyn's relatively low level of support from his party's MPs.

Villagers in Crickhowell, who launched their own bid to buy the Corn Exchange building, have successfully secured an agreement with Punch Taverns to purchase the property for £300,000 plus VAT, with plans to turn it into independent shops and flats, and about 180 people will become joint-owners after the deal is signed.

Alexis Scott, a 39-year-old former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted of theft and misfeasance after targeting long-haul passengers at Gatwick Airport's North Terminal in April 2013, tricking them into handing over cash they believed was in excess of the allowed £1,000 limit, resulting in £13,500 in losses.

TrueTube, an educational platform, and Horrible Histories are among the nominees for the Bafta Children's Awards, with TrueTube being named a contender for three awards, including best drama and the learning award.

The artworks of Sir Winston Churchill, including over 500 paintings, have been allocated to the National Trust, the Houses of Parliament, and the Churchill War Rooms in lieu of inheritance tax, with many of them remaining at Chartwell, Churchill's family home in Kent.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative activist and founder of the Eagle Forum, has died, leaving behind a legacy as a strong advocate for traditional family values and an outspoken critic of feminism, and being credited by some as a key figure in helping to usher in a new conservative era in US politics.

Wales international back, Morgan, will leave Bristol at the end of the season to move to a new team in Wales, primarily playing at full-back, in order to develop his skills and test himself for Wales.

England, seeking to secure their place in the World Twenty20 semi-finals, will face Sri Lanka in a must-win game on Saturday, which they need to win to progress.

Norway secured a 3-0 win over Northern Ireland in a friendly match, with goals coming from Nordtveit, Elyounoussi, and Ruud, as the visitors dominated the second half and secured their first win in 14 friendly matches.

Belgium's capital, Brussels, remains on high alert with hundreds of police and soldiers on patrol, amid fears of potential Paris-style attacks, after five people were charged in Belgium with terrorism offences in connection with the Paris attacks, including Mohamed Abrini who was seen driving a car used in the attacks.

Sheffield City Council has sent a "pre-action protocol letter" to Green Party councillor Alison Teal, warning that it will seek a High Court injunction to stop her and others from participating in future "direct action" against the council's tree removal efforts.

The Ospreys rugby team has signed 32-year-old Brian Mujati, a seasoned tight head prop, to provide injury cover and experience, particularly with key players Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia currently sidelined.

Gwynedd council "decided to go ahead" with establishing a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, where 500 people have signed a petition against the move and the school's governors want the site to be designated as a community site.

Oxfordshire County Council's proposal for a unitary council is based on two independent studies that found it could save £100m over five years, but the plan is opposed by the county's five district councils, who argue in favour of a different devolution model with an elected mayor.

Edinburgh Rugby's coach Dickinson has stated that his team must win all five of their remaining "huge games" to have a shout of the play-offs or the top six, as they face a tough run-in with matches against Newport Gwent Dragons, Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues.

Volunteers from the Northern Ireland Bat Group are hand-raising and rehabilitating large numbers of grounded and injured juvenile bats, which have been affected by the poor summer weather, with many being abandoned by their mothers due to difficulties in feeding and finding food.

Remains of a man, aged between 30 and 49, were discovered near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, with investigators still unable to determine the cause of death or the circumstances surrounding the discovery, which may have occurred up to three years prior.

A petition set up by hospital staff and residents opposes plans by Reading Borough Council to introduce pay and display meters and restrictions on parking in the area around the Royal Berkshire Hospital, citing concerns about increased parking pressures and difficulties for staff and patients.

A US Navy petty officer, Aimee Mejia, was involved in a three-car accident on the Japanese island of Okinawa, with alcohol levels about six times the permissible level, leading the US Navy to impose a temporary ban on drinking for personnel and additional training to promote responsible behavior.

The Lions, a team coached by Andy Flower, achieved a successful tri-series with impressive performances from batsmen such as Duckett, Bell-Drummond, Malan, and Billings, who all scored over 150 in various fixtures, potentially catching the attention of international selectors.

The Colombian government and the Farc rebel group agreed to resume peace negotiations in Havana, with a joint statement announcing the talks would take place from 10 to 17 December, and reconvene around mid-January, with a focus on a de-escalation of the conflict, meeting the relatives of victims, and establishing a permanent system to deal with future crises, following the release of three Colombian captives on Sunday.

Over 500 people participated in a march through Oxford to protest Oxfordshire County Council's plan to save £8m, with Prime Minister David Cameron having been invited to join the protest after expressing disappointment with the proposed changes to children's centre provision.

Devon and Cornwall Police's sandcastle depicting a murder victim, which won the Cornwall Beach Games competition, has sparked controversy and criticism for potentially trivializing a serious matter and being in poor taste.

Leyton Orient manager Ross Slade expressed optimism about the club's future, citing a potential change in structure and the new owner's willingness to invest in the team to strengthen the squad and improve results.

Buckinghamshire golfer Tyrrell Hatton secured his fifth top-10 finish in 13 European Tour events, finishing a shot behind the victorious Swede Alex Noren at the Scottish Open, and earned spots at the USPGA at Baltusrol and the Open Championship at Royal Troon.

A woman who was allegedly abused as a child testified in court that she was picked up from a children's home and abused by Basharat Hussain and others, who took her to Blackpool aged 12 and subjected her to various forms of abuse.
Franck Petricola, a 32-year-old road racer, died in a crash at Sulby Crossroads, becoming the 141st fatality at the event since it began in 1907.

Honda Racing team bosses have confirmed that Guy Martin will not be returning to the Ulster Grand Prix following his crash at the Isle of Man TT in June, in which the team has also experienced mechanical difficulties this year.
President Barack Obama has declared Louisiana a disaster area after severe flooding caused by torrential rain, with over 20,000 people rescued and some still stuck in their homes.

US Soccer has introduced new safety measures, including limiting heading in practice for children aged 11-13 and modifying substitution rules for concussions, in response to a concussion lawsuit filed by parents and young players.

A scandal has emerged in France's UMP party, with allegations that the party ordered nearly 11 million euros worth of fake invoices to cover overspends, which could damage the party and complicate any efforts by former president Nicolas Sarkozy, who is rumoured to be preparing to make a comeback in 2017.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders reported a decline in repossessions and arrears in the UK, with 2,500 homes repossessed in April, May, and June, down from 3,000 in the previous quarter and 5,400 in the same period last year, due to the supportive effect of low interest rates, and lenders are warning homeowners to prepare for a potential future rate rise.

Coventry accepted 159 people under the UK Government's expanded Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme, as part of the 1,602 Syrians resettled in the six months since October, with UKIP MEP James Carver expressing concerns about the pressure on local services.

Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff announced plans to organize a safe and successful Olympic Games in Rio, highlighting the torch relay, which will begin in May and cover over 300 Brazilian cities, and addressing concerns over security and water pollution.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's electoral reform, which guarantees a majority of seats to the party winning the most votes, has been approved by the lower house of parliament, with critics arguing it consolidates power and undermines democracy.
A 20-year-old Ajax player, Abdelhak Nouri, has suffered severe brain damage due to cardiac arrhythmias and a lack of oxygen supply during a game, with his chances of recovery described as nil.

Mani Dad's mother has launched a family court case and appealed to the public to help find her son, who disappeared from her home in Poland early this year and is believed to be living with his father, Zayn Dean, in the UK.

Dual citizens from certain nationalities, including Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan, must instead apply for a visa at the US embassy under new laws, with the implementation and clarity of the rules being unclear.

Sky is experiencing capacity issues at some of its telephone exchanges due to increased network traffic and new customer additions, which may be exacerbated by the recent launch of its Sky Go Extra service that allows users to download content for offline viewing.

The Scottish Prison Service is implementing legislation allowing it to use technology to disrupt prisoners' use of mobile phones at two pilot sites, HMP Shotts and Glenochil, with the technology scheduled to be operational by the end of the current financial year.

Leaders and survivors from around the world marked the 70th anniversary of the liberation of Nazi concentration camps, including Natzweiler-Struthof in France and Bergen-Belsen in Germany, where thousands of people were killed, including Jews, gypsies, and French resistance fighters.

Leigh led 18-0 at half-time against Salford, a result that means Widnes Vikings finish bottom of the Super League, while Salford drops to fourth place due to Hull FC's win over Huddersfield, and Leigh builds momentum ahead of the Super 8 qualifiers.

Billionaire Paul Allen is leading a project called Stratolaunch Systems, in collaboration with aerospace pioneer Burt Rutan, to develop a giant aircraft that can launch unmanned rockets into space from the air, with the goal of ferrying cargo and eventually undertaking manned missions.
Lancashire built a 264-run lead against Derbyshire, who ended the day on 27-2, setting up a competitive second day.

Jon Stewart hosted his final episode of The Daily Show, a popular satirical news program on Comedy Central, after a successful run, during which he established himself as one of the most influential satirists in the US and the voice of liberal America, and helped launch the careers of notable comedians like Steve Carell, John Oliver, and Stephen Colbert, who took over the show in 1999.
Nottingham Forest, a four-time League Cup winner, are seeking to progress past the third round of the competition for the first time in 11 seasons to earn a spot in the Europa League.
The Arches, a Glasgow venue, has gone into administration after a midnight closing time imposed by the city's licensing board cut its total revenues by more than 50%, putting 130 jobs at risk.

Ivor Bell, a 77-year-old former senior leader in the Provisional IRA, has been charged with aiding and abetting murder and membership of the IRA in relation to the 1972 disappearance and murder of Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" victims of the Troubles.
Wigan Warriors scored 21 unanswered points to triumph after going down to 12 men, and victory next week against Catalans Dragons would guarantee them a home semi-final.

Yorkshire Sculpture Park has seen a 170% rise in visitor numbers, with 100,000 people visiting in September when the poppy installation, Wave, was on display, as part of a nationwide tour commemorating the centenary of World War One.

The A361 road in Somerset, England, which was closed due to flooding, has reopened after a severe flood warning was lifted, with temporary traffic lights to be installed to ensure safe passage, and a further inspection planned to remove the lights once the road is deemed safe.
Scientists using Japan's Subaru telescope have discovered an icy body, catalogued as V774104, which is approximately 15.5 billion kilometers from the Sun, about three times further away than Pluto.

Ashley Yates, the head of The Tynings Primary School in South Gloucestershire, has admitted to making indecent images of children and voyeurism, and additional adult victims have been identified after items were seized by police during the investigation.

Strictly Come Dancing contestants Steve and Ola Jordan have spoken out about the "bullying" claims that were made against them, saying that in response, they chose to show unity and not dignify the allegations with a response.

The UK's inflation rate dropped to 2.6% in June, contrary to economists' expectations of no change, leading to a decline in the value of the pound and causing a slight drop in the FTSE 100 share index.

British actress Vicky McClure was mistakenly thrown off a tram in Nottingham in 2015 after a conductor, unaware of her free travel offer due to a ceremony naming a tram in her honor, asked her for a ticket.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross, found murdered in a London river in 2014, will investigate whether government and police failures contributed to her death and allowed the chief suspect, a Latvian builder with a murder conviction, to live unchecked in the UK.

A study by The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling found that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate dropped from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest rate of all Scottish towns at 33% and Inverurie having the lowest rate at 1%.

Rory McWhirter, a man from Edinburgh, was sentenced to custody for a "fairly sophisticated" fraudulent scheme in which he used fake births and marriage certificates to claim £14,222 in tax credits, £19,658 in child benefits, and a £500 maternity grant.
